 The Absolute Batman #25 Clay Mann Cover Jumps From $8 To $60 In A Day 
 Posted in: Batman , Comics , DC Comics | Tagged: 
 The Absolute Batman #25 Clay Mann Cover Jumps From $8 To $60 In A Day
 The Absolute Batman #25 open order Clay Mann foil cover jumps from $8 to $60 in one day on eBay
 Published Thu, 29 Oct 2026 18:00:08 -0500 by Rich Johnston | Last updated Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:34:54 -0500 | Comments Article Summary
 Absolute Batman #25’s open-order Clay Mann foil variant surged from its $8.99 cover price to $60 eBay sales in 24 hours.
 Signed Absolute Batman #25 Clay Mann copies have also hit $100 on eBay, signaling intense collector demand right after release.
 Despite a massive 775,000-copy print run, Lunar Distribution reportedly sold out of the Absolute Batman #25 foil cover.
 The manga-style Absolute Batman #25 cover echoes Weekly Shonen Jump aesthetics, following Mann’s hot Chainsaw Man-style variant.
 Absolute Batman #25 by Scott Snyder and Nick Dragotta was published yesterday by DC Comics, with over 775,000 copies printed. It may not have been enough. The open-order Clay Mann foil cover, reflecting the comics' manga aesthetic, turning the book into a fake Japanese monthly manga magazine that clearly got a lot of attention, even at a $9 price tag. But maybe they could have charged more, as copies have now sold on eBay for $60. and signed copies by Clay Mann for $100 . Naturally, Lunar Distribution are all out of copies, and have been apologising to retailers who have asked.
 Absolute Batman #25 Clay Mann Cover 
 Styled after anthology magazines like Weekly Shōnen Jump , the cover has "DC Comics Presents" at the top in Japanese, giant side text shouts "Popular characters assemble!!" Catwoman gets prominent billing next to Batman with text about the strongest pairing finally appearing together. Inset panels tease "Enemy or ally… or are they lovers!?!?" Credits are done in classic manga fashion, listing The Mannboyz and Dragotta over "the exciting original" by Scott Snyder, complete with a goat badge next to Dragotta's name calling him "the GOAT." It's not the first time The Mannboyz have gone manga with Absolute Batman . Their earlier variant for issue #18 recreated the look of Chainsaw Man Volume 1, giving Batman chainsaw hands. That one sold out quickly, and the Absolute Batman #25 magazine treatment has drawn similar collector interest without breaking any of DC Comics' new cover guidelines . Even so, to go from an $8 comic to repeat $60 sales in just one day, for an open-order comic book cover with such a high print run, well that is new…
